messages:
hannah: Quick callout: onboarding a new engineer on the JS SDK + Expo (Hermes) and ran into a combo of issues. Metro picked the ESM export and then runtime blew up (global.crypto undefined, ReadableStream missing). Also hit TS errors because types import node:stream. Anyone documented minimal steps for a sample app?
omar: Yep, classic. If package.json has `exports.import` pointing to .mjs Metro will prefer that. Two pragmatic options: add a `react-native` field to package.json pointing at a CJS build, or add a Metro alias in the app to force the CJS file.
hannah: I can do the alias in the sample app but we want the official quickstart to "just work" for Expo users. The docs currently just show `import SDK from 'acme-sdk'`. New devs hit cryptic Hermes errors and file a support ticket.
kevin: For a one-off repro we did this metro snippet:```js
// metro.config.js
const path = require('path')
module.exports = { resolver: { extraNodeModules: { 'acme-sdk$': path.resolve(__dirname, 'node_modules/acme-sdk/dist/index.cjs') } } }
```
aditya: Runtime shims we add at app entry: `import 'react-native-get-random-values'; import 'abortcontroller-polyfill/dist/abortcontroller-polyfill-only';` plus `const { ReadableStream } = require('web-streams-polyfill/ponyfill'); if (!global.ReadableStream) global.ReadableStream = ReadableStream;` Also Hermes sometimes needs a `Symbol.asyncIterator` polyfill: `if (!Symbol.asyncIterator) Symbol.asyncIterator = Symbol.for('asyncIterator')`.
hannah: TS is the other headache. The SDK d.ts references `node:stream` and tsc drags in the Node lib DOM/stream types which then breaks RN builds. We hacked `skipLibCheck` in tsconfig to get past it. Ugly.
omar: Upstream asks we recommend: 1) publish a `react-native` entry or ensure `main` resolves to CJS for packagers that prefer require, 2) provide separate `.d.ts` files for browser/RN that avoid `node:` imports, 3) publish a lightweight browser/UMD or RN bundle that omits Node-only adapters, 4) add an `examples/expo` sample prewired with shims and a short onboarding doc.
kevin: Also propose tiny runtime flags (build-time) to opt-out of streaming or node adapters so the RN bundle can be small and tree-shakeable. That allows a single codebase but different bundles for node/browser/RN.
aditya: For the issue/PR I'll attach a minimal repro: expo init blank -> enable Hermes -> add SDK + `react-native-get-random-values web-streams-polyfill abortcontroller-polyfill` -> top-of-App imports for shims -> run -> observe crash. Include metro log showing picked mjs and the tsc output for the Node type leak.
hannah: Perfect. One more detail—some users reported that even with web-streams-polyfill the SDK's `for await` loops still fail on Hermes because the polyfill doesn't wire the async iterator in all code paths. We added a tiny adapter that wraps iterables: `async function* toAsyncIterator(iter) { for await (const v of iter) yield v }` and used that around the problematic call sites in a local fork. Worth mentioning in repro.
omar: Good note. For short-term support replies we should add a one-paragraph "Expo gotchas" to the docs listing: metro alias / require CJS, install 3 polyfills, tsconfig skipLibCheck, Symbol.asyncIterator shim, and explicit require fallback if alias isn't possible.
aditya: I'll draft the GH issue with the checklist + repro + proposed PR that adds a `react-native` build and example. I'll paste the draft here before opening.
expo-bot: FYI — Expo SDK 48+ surfaces `crypto.getRandomValues` in managed runtimes; dev clients and older SDKs may still need manual polyfills. See https://blog.expo.dev/ for details.
hannah: Thanks everyone — this should reduce new-dev friction if we get the sample and doc changes in. I'll hold off filing until aditya posts the draft. :thumbsup:
